Enumerated project pages and retained nested comment blocks, including archived pages.
Enumerated repositories, issues, pull requests, reviews, and retained discussion replies.

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: February planning: Lanternleaf will test whether royalty-statement exceptions can be reviewed from one queue instead of three spreadsheets. Contributor 01 is taking the exception rules and prototype; Contributor 07 owns the source export. Pilot is two imprints only.
records.title: Lanternleaf kickoff note

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Pilot brief. Problem: reviewers reconcile duplicate, negative, and unusually large royalty lines across separate exports. Scope: two imprints, quarterly statements, advisory flags only. No automatic payment holds. Success measures: reviewer time, missed known exceptions, and false alerts. Decisions remain with Publishing Operations.
records.title: Lanternleaf pilot brief

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Could you include contract currency and reversal reference in the sample export? I can draft rules against the current columns, but negative lines without their reversal IDs will look like genuine exceptions.
records.title: Export fields request

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: Currency is available. Reversal reference is not in the scheduled feed; I can add it to the one-off pilot extract, but production needs a finance-system change.
records.title: Re: Export fields request

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Draft taxonomy: exact duplicate, probable reversal pair, negative without visible pair, and high-value outlier. Proposed output includes rule code and a plain-language reason. Thresholds are provisional until Operations labels a sample. Known limitation: reversal matching depends on an optional reference or, failing that, amount/date heuristics.
records.title: Exception taxonomy v0.1

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: Comment: please separate a true duplicate from two editions earning the same amount. Title-level matching caused false alarms in last year's manual check.
records.title: Comment on exception taxonomy

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Agreed. Revised duplicate key is contract, edition, territory, period, amount, and transaction type. Same-title matches are no longer sufficient. I also added an “insufficient fields” reason rather than guessing.
records.title: Reply: revised duplicate key

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Implements four advisory exception rules, reason codes, and fixture-based tests. Reversal matching prefers reference IDs and falls back to same contract, inverse amount, and a 45-day window. Outlier threshold is configuration, not hard-coded.
records.title: PR 18: initial exception engine

records.author: Contributor 09
records.body: The fallback pairs across currencies because the comparison normalises neither currency nor amount. A £500 line could cancel a €500 line.
records.title: Review: currency pairing defect

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Fixed by requiring equal currency before inverse-amount matching; added mixed-currency fixtures. I also made missing currency return “insufficient fields.”
records.title: Reply: currency guard added

records.author: Contributor 09
records.body: Retested. Mixed currencies no longer pair. Approved, with the broader concern that 45 days may be too permissive until we see labelled data.
records.title: Approval after correction

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Prototype queue is on the test workspace. Filters are imprint, quarter, and reason; selecting a row shows the source fields used by the rule. It does not update payment status. Please use the feedback sheet for incorrect flags.
records.title: Prototype available

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Pilot feedback sheet. Reviewers should label each sampled flag as useful, incorrect, or unclear and record minutes spent. The original reviewer-by-reviewer export is attached for audit, but its retained copy cannot be opened.
records.title: Pilot feedback instructions

records.author: Contributor 11
records.body: The east-window fern has been moved away from the radiator. Please stop adding coffee grounds; the compost bin is downstairs.
records.title: Fern update

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: First pass: the reason text is much better than raw codes. Eleven “negative without pair” flags are all from the same backdated correction batch, so they are technically correct but not useful individually.
records.title: First reviewer feedback

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: I can group those by correction batch if the batch identifier is stable. Otherwise I can suppress identical contract/date reasons into one expandable group without changing the underlying flags.
records.title: Proposed grouping

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: Batch ID is stable in the one-off extract but not guaranteed in the scheduled feed. Grouping in the view is safer than making it part of rule identity.
records.title: Batch identifier caveat

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Groups repeated flags by contract, posting date, and reason in the queue while preserving each underlying line. Adds expand/collapse and an accessible group count. No rule suppression.
records.title: PR 23: repeated-flag grouping

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Keyboard focus disappears after collapsing a group. Please return focus to the group header.
records.title: Review: focus regression

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Updated collapse behavior to retain focus on the header and added a keyboard test. Ready for another pass.
records.title: Reply: focus behavior fixed

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: Timed comparison, 24 sampled statements across the two pilot imprints: current process median 19 minutes; Lanternleaf-assisted median 12 minutes. Four reviewers participated. Samples were selected from statements already suspected to contain exceptions, so this is not a general workload estimate.
records.title: Pilot timing note

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: Label review: 63 flags checked; 45 useful, 12 incorrect, 6 unclear. Most incorrect flags came from heuristic reversal matching where the reference was absent. Exact duplicates had no incorrect labels in this sample. Counts combine four reviewers and are not an independent audit.
records.title: Flag-label summary

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Proposal based on pilot labels: shorten reference-free reversal window from 45 to 14 days and expose the match basis in the queue. This reduces questionable pairings but may leave legitimate late reversals flagged.
records.title: Issue 31: tighten reversal heuristic

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: Fourteen days fits the sampled correction batches, but annual adjustments can arrive after a month. Could those remain “uncertain” instead of being treated as unmatched negatives?
records.title: Operations concern on late reversals

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Yes. Revised plan: confident pairs within 14 days; 15–45 day inverse matches become “possible late reversal” and stay visible. Beyond 45 days remains unmatched. That avoids silently clearing them.
records.title: Reply: three-state reversal handling

records.author: Contributor 10
records.body: Implemented Issue 31’s three-state reversal handling and match-basis display, using Contributor 01’s design and tests from the issue branch. Contributor 01 reviewed the final change; I handled the production integration conflicts.
records.title: PR 29: reversal confidence states

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Decision: continue through the April statement run. Contributor 01, please document monitoring and train the two shift leads. Wider imprint rollout is not approved yet; Finance still needs to decide whether reversal reference can enter the scheduled feed.
records.title: April continuation decision

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Runbook: load validation, rule-version check, queue health checks, rollback to spreadsheet review, and escalation contacts by role. Daily checks cover missing currency, unexpected flag-volume changes, and stale source timestamps. The tool remains advisory.
records.title: Pilot operations runbook

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: Training note: Contributor 01 ran a 35-minute walkthrough for both shift leads using a staged statement. We practised expanding grouped flags, reading match basis, and falling back to the spreadsheet. Both leads completed the exercise; ordinary reviewers were not trained in this session.
records.title: Shift-lead training record

records.author: Contributor 12
records.body: After the source export changed `statement_period` from text to a date, the queue loaded zero rows without an error. April processing was delayed for about two hours while we reverted to the spreadsheet.
records.title: Issue 38: silent zero-row load

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: I assumed the pilot schema would remain fixed and validated required columns but not their types. I’m adding type checks and a visible stop condition; the runbook fallback limited the delay, but the silent success was my miss.
records.title: Cause and corrective action

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: The export change was mine and I did not notify the pilot channel because the field name was unchanged. Type validation is still needed, but change notice also failed here.
records.title: Reply: shared cause

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Adds schema type validation, blocks processing on incompatible fields, and displays the received versus expected type. Includes the April export shape as a regression fixture.
records.title: PR 34: fail closed on schema mismatch

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: April run finished. We used the queue after the schema fix and kept the spreadsheet open for the first hour. No further load failures. The grouping made the correction batch manageable, though one lead still exported rows to annotate them.
records.title: April run completed

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Window close summary: Contributor 01 designed the exception taxonomy, built the initial engine and queue grouping, responded to review defects, authored the runbook, and trained shift leads. Contributor 10 integrated the revised reversal states; Contributor 07 owned exports. April completed after one two-hour schema incident. Recommendation: limited continuation, not general rollout.
records.title: Pilot close summary

records.author: Contributor 02
records.body: Summer lunch poll closes Friday. The courtyard option has shade but only six covered tables.
records.title: Lunch poll reminder

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: May follow-up, same two imprints: 41 statements processed with Lanternleaf available; 34 were reviewed primarily in the queue and 7 primarily in spreadsheets. Median recorded review time was 13 minutes, but eight statements lacked usable timing entries. No missed-exception audit was performed.
records.title: May operational follow-up

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: Both shift leads are still using it. Two of six ordinary reviewers now open the queue themselves; the others receive exports or stay in the spreadsheet. That is local use, not rollout to the other imprints.
records.title: Adoption check

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Finance has deferred adding reversal reference to the scheduled feed until its autumn planning round. The pilot can continue with confidence states, but false-alert performance remains dependent on heuristic matching. No owner or date exists for broader rollout.
records.title: Dependency status

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Request from one shift lead: bulk notes for grouped flags. Marking as backlog because current annotations still live in the spreadsheet export. This is an inconvenience, not a processing blocker.
records.title: Issue 52: bulk group notes

records.author: Contributor 14
records.body: Next month's selection is the shorter of the two proposed novels. Spare copies are in the blue cupboard.
records.title: Book club selection

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: August planning approved extending Lanternleaf to a third imprint in October, contingent on an assigned support rotation. Contributor 01 is not scheduled to lead that extension.
records.title: Post-horizon extension decision
